Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Wood vs. the lunch line. Truffaut to a lunch lady. Corn. Panel 1: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat leaning over a cafeteria tray toward a bored lunch lady with a ladle, serving line with a sneeze guard and a heat lamp, fluorescent glare, 1990s high school cafeteria. Wood says "Do you ever consider that this room is the only place in Small Wood where three hundred people voluntarily sit in the same direction?". Panel 2: close two-shot across a cafeteria counter, a lunch lady with a raised ladle giving a flat stare to a gaunt teenage boy in an overcoat, steam rising. Lunch Lady says "Corn or peas.". Panel 3: a teenage boy in a wool overcoat holding a cafeteria tray turns to face the viewer declaiming, the lunch line moving on behind him, heavy black shadows. Wood says "Truffaut said the film of tomorrow will be an act of love. I said corn.". Panel 4: wide shot of a long empty cafeteria table, a teenage boy in an overcoat alone at the near end with a plate of corn, far in the background a boy in a backwards cap drawing on a napkin and a girl with headphones reading, rain on tall windows, lots of empty table. No dialogue in this panel. In the bottom right margin, tiny hand-lettered signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes.

Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A dollar goes in. Nothing comes out. Wood takes it personally, then philosophically. Panel 1: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat carefully feeding a limp dollar bill into a school vending machine, harsh fluorescent light. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: close-up inside a vending machine window, the metal coil turned and a bag of chips hanging caught on the edge, not falling. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy pressing his forehead and both hands against the glass of a vending machine while a student passes behind him. Wood says "This machine has taken my dollar and given me a lesson about desire. That is not what I asked for.". Panel 4: a teenage boy alone at a vending machine, his face reflected in the glass beside a hanging bag of chips, empty cafeteria behind, heavy black spotting. Wood says, in a small balloon, "Fine. Panel 4: a teenage boy in an overcoat looking with surprise at a drawing held by a boy in a backwards cap who is already drawing the next one, gym assembly below. Wood says "...That's actually—". Gully says "Yeah.".
